questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\{\begin{aligned}x=5-2t \\ y=-1+4t \\ z=-3-5t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:2x-5y+3z-84=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-5y+3z-84 & =0 \\ 2(5-2t)-5(-1+4t)+3(-3-5t) & =84 \\ 10-4t+5-20t-9-15t & =84 \\ -39t & =78 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-2$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=5-2(-2)=9 \\ y=-1+4(-2)=-9 \\ z=-3-5(-2)=7\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(9,-9,7).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\{\begin{aligned}x=-2-2t \\ y=5-3t \\ z=-1+2t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:3x-2y+6z=62.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}3x-2y+6z & =62 \\ 3(-2-2t)-2(5-3t)+6(-1+2t) & =62 \\ -6-6t-10+6t-6+12t & =62 \\ 12t & =84 \\ t & =7\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=6$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=-2-2(7)=-16 \\ y=5-3(7)=-16 \\ z=-1+2(7)=13\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $P(-16,-16,13).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:\{\begin{aligned}x=3-5t \\ y=2-3t \\ z=-2-6t\end{aligned}\,\text{and}\,Π:5x-2y+4z-132=0.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We can substitute the parametric expressions for $x,$ $y,$ and $z$ of the line into the equation of the plane immediately:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-2y+4z-132 & =0 \\ 5(3-5t)-2(2-3t)+4(-2-6t) & =132 \\ 15-25t-4+6t-8-24t & =132 \\ -43t & =129 \\ t & =-3\end{aligned}
$$

To get the position vector $p$ of the intersection point $P$, we substitute $t=-3$ into the parametric equations of the line:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}x=3-5(-3)=18 \\ y=2-3(-3)=11 \\ z=-2-6(-3)=16\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is  $P(18,11,16).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩,\,Π:r=⟨-5,4,2⟩+s⟨0,3,1⟩+t⟨2,0,1⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨0,3,1⟩\times ⟨2,0,1⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =3i+2j-6k \\  & =⟨3,2,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =⟨-5,4,2⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨3,1,5⟩+w⟨-2,-5,4⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ ⟨3-2w,1-5w,5+4w⟩\cdot ⟨3,2,-6⟩ & =-19 \\ 3(3-2w)+2(1-5w)-6(5+4w) & =-19 \\ 9-6w+2-10w-30-24w & =-19 \\ -40w & =0 \\ w & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=0$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨3-2(0),1-5(0),5+4(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨3,1,5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(3,1,5).$

questions.problem:
Find the intersection point of the line $l$ and the plane $Π$ with equations

$$
l:r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩,\,Π:r=⟨5,3,-4⟩+s⟨1,0,2⟩+t⟨0,-2,3⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
From the equation of a plane in the parametric form $r=p+tv+sw$, we have that its normal vector is $n=v\times w.$ In our case, the normal vectors to $Π$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =v\times w \\  & =⟨1,0,2⟩\times ⟨0,-2,3⟩ \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -2 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =4i-3j-2k \\  & =⟨4,-3,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the plane $Π$ in dot product form is

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =⟨5,3,-4⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $r=⟨1,-1,2⟩+w⟨3,4,-1⟩$ into the equation of the plane in dot product form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ ⟨1+3w,-1+4w,2-w⟩\cdot ⟨4,-3,-2⟩ & =19 \\ 4(1+3w)-3(-1+4w)-2(2-w) & =19 \\ 4+12w+3-12w-4+2w & =19 \\ 2w & =16 \\ w & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to get the position vector $q$ of the intersection point $Q,$ we substitute $w=8$ into the equation of the line:

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨1+3(8),-1+4(8),2-8⟩ \\  & =⟨25,31,-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

So, the intersection point is $Q(25,31,-6).$
